name: Confucius
summary: Confucius, born Kong Qiu, was a Chinese philosopher of the Spring and Autumn period who is traditionally considered the paragon of Chinese sages.

facts.text: Confucius taught that good government begins with moral example, not only punishment and rules.
facts.context: Confucius makes leadership personal: people notice what leaders practice before they trust what leaders command.

facts.text: Confucius's philosophical teachings, called Confucianism, emphasized personal and governmental morality, harmonious social relationships, righteousness, kindness, sincerity, and a ruler's responsibilities to lead by virtue.
